name: /work
description: Load context and identify next task

steps.description: Collect coverage, recent memory, pattern hint and local Git once in one Python process; no network or writes.

steps.action: Format and display the work brief
steps.context:
You are producing a work brief to re-orient the user into this project only. Use the collected project-local Git state and TODO before generating the brief. Do not query a cross-project index, hub, vault, or external memory.

Generate a rich, structured brief in this order:

1. RIGHT NOW - reconcile right_now against later events and live Git before describing current state. Quote historical actions as historical; do not promote a completed, cancelled, or rolled-back item into current work. If it contains insufficient recent context, read at most the two newest project-local `.exocortex/events/*.md` files and reconstruct the last work, decisions, next actions, and blockers.

2. SHORT-TERM - summarize shortterm as dated evidence, with source references and unresolved contradictions.

3. SUBCONSCIOUS NUDGE - display subconscious_nudge if non-empty.

4. GIT STATE - use the returned Git status/branch and recent commits. List each modified or untracked path and flag a branch that appears pending integration. A working tree can be shared with another session, so say plainly which listed paths this session did not create; treat every one of them as another writer's work.

5. OPEN ITEMS - read project-local `.exocortex/OPEN_DECISIONS.md` when present and identify unresolved decisions or overdue local actions.

6. NEXT TASK - show the first incomplete task group from the Ready section of `.exocortex/TODO.md`.

Then show the A/B/C choice. Name actual local evidence and identify uncertainty instead of guessing.

If the human chooses B, stage only the paths this session changed, naming each one explicitly. Never run `git add -A` or `git add .`, and never stage a path this session did not create: in a shared working tree that commits another writer's work under this session's name. If ownership of any listed path is unclear, say so and commit nothing until the human resolves it. Offering B is not authority to commit, and it never authorizes push, merge, deployment, or synchronization.
Reuse returned Git and note evidence; do not rerun the helpers or freshness check. Report coverage status, omitted events and truncated excerpts; inspect only source files needed to resolve material uncertainty. Never treat omitted history as reviewed.

options: B) Commit this session's own changes first
